title: Estar: Tras el telón
author: Cuentiva · verb story
summary: Location and how someone feels or is doing. Six present-indicative forms; vosotros is used in Spain.

verbFocus.scope: Location and how someone feels or is doing. Six present-indicative forms; vosotros is used in Spain.

sentences.spanish: Antes de la función, estar cuenta dónde está cada persona y cómo se siente.
sentences.english: Before the performance, estar tells us where each person is and how they feel.

sentences.spanish: «Estoy detrás del telón y estoy muy nerviosa», dice Inés por teléfono.
sentences.english: “I am behind the curtain and I am very nervous,” Inés says on the phone.

sentences.spanish: Su hermano pregunta: «¿Estás sola o estás con los demás?».
sentences.english: Her brother asks, “Are you alone or are you with the others?”

sentences.spanish: «La directora está aquí, pero mi vestido no está en su sitio».

sentences.spanish: Dos actores llegan corriendo: «Estamos listos, pero estamos preocupados por ti».

sentences.spanish: La directora pregunta: «¿Estáis seguros de que habéis mirado en todas las cajas?».

sentences.spanish: «Los vestidos están allí, pero las cajas están cerradas», responde un actor.

sentences.spanish: Inés grita: «¡Estoy cansada de buscar y el público ya está dentro!».

sentences.spanish: La directora baja la voz: «Estás asustada; vamos a buscar juntas».
sentences.english: The director lowers her voice: “You are frightened; let us look together.”

sentences.spanish: «Estamos contigo», repiten los actores mientras apartan las sillas.

sentences.spanish: Entonces Inés ve una esquina roja debajo de una mesa.

sentences.spanish: El vestido está allí, junto a una nota que no reconoce.
sentences.english: The dress is there, beside a note she does not recognize.

continuation.spanish: Inés vuelve a llamarlo: «¿Estás en el teatro de verdad?».

continuation.spanish: «Sí, mi asiento está en la primera fila».
continuation.english: “Yes, my seat is in the front row.”

continuation.spanish: Inés mira a sus compañeros: «Estamos a tiempo; todavía podemos salir».

continuation.spanish: Las luces están encendidas y las puertas están cerradas.

continuation.spanish: «Estoy nerviosa todavía», admite Inés mientras se pone el vestido.
continuation.english: “I am still nervous,” Inés admits as she puts on the dress.

continuation.spanish: «Estás aquí, y eso es suficiente para empezar», responde su amiga.
continuation.english: “You are here, and that is enough to begin,” her friend replies.

continuation.spanish: Cuando se abre el telón, Inés ve que su hermano está sonriendo.
continuation.english: When the curtain opens, Inés sees that her brother is smiling.

continuation.spanish: «Estamos juntos», piensa, aunque él esté entre el público.
continuation.english: “We are together,” she thinks, even though he is in the audience.

continuation.spanish: Estar le ha servido para pedir ayuda, encontrar el vestido y expresar su miedo.
continuation.english: Estar has helped her ask for help, find the dress, and express her fear.

continuation.spanish: Ahora está en el escenario y empieza su primera frase.
continuation.english: Now she is on stage and begins her first line.

title: Querer: La última cena
author: Cuentiva · verb story
summary: Wants, wishes, and affection. Six present-indicative forms; vosotros is used in Spain.

verbFocus.scope: Wants, wishes, and affection. Six present-indicative forms; vosotros is used in Spain.

sentences.spanish: En la última cena antes del viaje, querer expresa deseos y también cariño.
sentences.english: At the last dinner before the journey, querer expresses wishes and also affection.

sentences.spanish: «Quiero irme, pero no quiero haceros daño», dice Lucas.
sentences.english: “I want to leave, but I do not want to hurt you,” Lucas says.

sentences.spanish: Su hermana pregunta: «¿Quieres viajar o quieres escapar de nosotros?».
sentences.english: His sister asks, “Do you want to travel or do you want to escape from us?”

sentences.spanish: Su padre interviene: «Él quiere conocer otros lugares».
sentences.english: His father steps in: “He wants to get to know other places.”

sentences.spanish: «Queremos entenderte, pero también queremos verte», dice su madre.
sentences.english: “We want to understand you, but we also want to see you,” his mother says.

sentences.spanish: Lucas responde: «Queréis que sea feliz, pero os cuesta dejarme salir».
sentences.english: Lucas replies, “You want me to be happy, but it is hard for you to let me leave.”

sentences.spanish: Sus abuelos escuchan desde el sofá; quieren hablar sin discutir.
sentences.english: His grandparents listen from the sofa; they want to talk without arguing.

sentences.spanish: La hermana aparta el plato: «Te quiero y no quiero perderte».
sentences.english: His sister pushes her plate aside: “I love you and I do not want to lose you.”

sentences.spanish: Lucas se queda callado porque no esperaba escuchar aquello.
sentences.english: Lucas falls silent because he did not expect to hear that.

sentences.spanish: Después dice: «Si quieres, podemos hablar cada domingo».
sentences.english: Then he says, “If you want, we can talk every Sunday.”

sentences.spanish: «No queremos una promesa imposible», responde su padre.
sentences.english: “We do not want an impossible promise,” his father replies.

sentences.spanish: Lucas deja el teléfono y pregunta qué necesita cada uno.
sentences.english: Lucas puts down his phone and asks what each person needs.

continuation.spanish: Su madre empieza: «Quiero saber cómo estás, incluso cuando tengas un mal día».
continuation.english: His mother begins, “I want to know how you are, even when you have a bad day.”

continuation.spanish: Lucas pregunta a su hermana: «¿Quieres enseñarme tus dibujos por videollamada?».
continuation.english: Lucas asks his sister, “Do you want to show me your drawings on a video call?”

continuation.spanish: Ella asiente; quiere compartir algo más que despedidas.
continuation.english: She nods; she wants to share more than goodbyes.

continuation.spanish: «Queremos que esta casa siga siendo tu casa», dicen sus padres.
continuation.english: “We want this house to remain your home,” his parents say.

continuation.spanish: «Y vosotros, ¿qué queréis que os traiga?», pregunta Lucas a sus abuelos.
continuation.english: “And what do you want me to bring you?” Lucas asks his grandparents.

continuation.spanish: Ellos no quieren regalos; quieren escuchar historias que él haya vivido.
continuation.english: They do not want presents; they want to hear stories he has lived through.

continuation.spanish: Lucas sonríe: «Quiero aprender a contarlas bien».
continuation.english: Lucas smiles: “I want to learn to tell them well.”

continuation.spanish: Su hermana se acerca: «Quieres vivir algo nuevo; ahora lo entiendo mejor».
continuation.english: His sister comes closer: “You want to experience something new; now I understand it better.”

continuation.spanish: La madre quiere una foto antes de que se enfríe la cena.
continuation.english: Their mother wants a photograph before dinner gets cold.

continuation.spanish: Todos quieren salir juntos en la imagen y acercan las sillas.
continuation.english: Everyone wants to be in the picture together and they move their chairs closer.

continuation.spanish: Querer no ha eliminado sus diferencias, pero les ha permitido decir qué les importa.
continuation.english: Querer has not removed their differences, but it has allowed them to say what matters to them.

continuation.spanish: «Os quiero», dice Lucas, y esta vez nadie necesita una explicación.
continuation.english: “I love you,” Lucas says, and this time nobody needs an explanation.
